summaryEn: Ice-shelled monsters swarm around {dungeon}; ordinary blades barely scratch them and hunters talk of smashing rather than cutting.
{dungeon} keeps erupting; anyone entering is exposed to long, intense heat and survival depends on what they wear.
A fast beast herd from {dungeon} roams the highway; travelers are told to protect themselves before setting out.

The hero took a quest above their level, received a large advance and plans to shop before departing.
The hero party may head to {dungeon}, home of fire-wreathed monsters, and prepares protection that counters searing fire attacks; plans are unsettled.

The hero is busy repaying debts and avoids expensive gear for the time being.
The Windcutter party bulk-bought wind-imbued weapons for a hunt against rock monsters.
A trading house in the next town is cornering protective gear that counters searing fire attacks of fire-wreathed monsters in {dungeon}.
A trading house in the next town is cornering protective gear that counters freezing water-and-ice attacks of monsters clad in water and ice in {dungeon}.
A trading house in the next town is cornering protective gear that counters wind-swift claws of beasts that run like the wind in {dungeon}.

A trading house in the next town is cornering protective gear that counters eye-searing light beams of machine soldiers emitting blinding light in {dungeon}.
Mercenaries in {region} reportedly gather dark weapons for a night hunt on light-emitting machine soldiers; single unnamed source.
A major arms dealer is dumping its stock of heavy stone-forged armor onto the market.
The Crimson band will hunt a storm bird wrapped in strong winds and means to burn it down.
A cave-in halted the mine in {region}, the main source of hard ore for heavy rock-like armor.
The cathedral postponed the blessing rite needed to finish armor carrying holy light.
Large logging in {region} floods the market with supple timber used for bows and spear shafts.
The sacred spring in {region} dried up; smiths cannot forge blades that carry flowing water.
A new fire-spirit furnace in {region} lets workshops turn out flame-imbued belts and helmets in bulk.
A pilgrim choir is passing through; custom says townsfolk greet it dressed in holy-light garb.
Rumor says the wind spirit festival, where people parade in light wind-blessed garb, is moved up; unconfirmed.
Figures seen at night in the old graveyard; if the dead are walking, only blades of purifying light will do.
A bard's new song about a black-clad knight makes dark-colored helmets and armor fashionable.
A flame dance troupe is coming; spectators traditionally wear flame-shaped sashes and belts.
The royal council passed a new tax on armor trading.
The crown created a bounty for monster hunting, drawing new adventurers who first need something to fight with.
A gold strike in {region} fills adventurers' purses and hunt rewards rise.
A major money changer closed; adventurers' cash is short and pricey purchases are put off.
A nearby village's watch decides to outfit its members with protective gear after night injuries.
Flooding brought slippery water monsters into village fields; heavy crushing blows are said to work.
Lizards with scorching breath infest the hot springs near {region}; the injured are burned rather than bitten.
A serpent with slick scales lurks in the lake near {region}; it seems made of water itself and blades slide off.
Harpies whipping up gusts attack travelers on a pass near {region}; most victims are clawed after being blown toward cliffs.
In {region}, creatures that melt into shadows strike night travelers with claws from the dark.
A ghost knight in dazzling armor haunts an old fort near {region}; its radiance blinds attackers and swallows their blows.
A giant of mud and rock near {region} shakes the ground and hurls stones; most injuries come from flying rocks.
The hero became a disciple of an old knight whose motto is to protect yourself before you strike.
Endless rain near {region} stops charcoal burning; forges cannot reach the fiercest heat needed for one kind of blade finishing.
Drought dries village fields and insects that spit embers swarm; hitting them scatters sparks.
Canal works in the capital halt the barges that carry hard northern ore, which workshops use most for rock-hard armor.
The lighthouse at {region} goes dark for repairs; old sailors say light-shunning shadows crawl ashore on lightless nights.
The royal mourning period ends; the black attire everyone wore, including dark helmets and armor, is no longer needed.
The hero courts a cathedral priest's daughter; the priest demands a suitor who wears holy protection against darkness.
An unknown monster near {region}: one report mentions a hard shell, another says axes bounce off something like rock and it must be cut from afar.
Hot-spring cures at the foot of {dungeon} become the rage; visitors venture near the scorching crater and come back blistered.
The adventurers' insurance union stops covering theft of expensive gear.
An ancient dragon in human form shops in town; it has a fever and seeks protection that cools its burning body.
A fortune teller claiming to be the Demon King tells everyone to beware of darkness and wear protection that repels it.
Gold coins rain from the sky over {region}; the lucky finders rush to buy top-class gear.
The hero puts down the sword to train as a bard; young adventurers imitate them and neglect weapons.
A legendary smith returns after ten years and declares he will forge only wind-cutting weapons; everyone wants one.
A crowned giant slime leads a parade of slimes down the highway; swords get swallowed, heavy crushing blows are needed.
A ghost peddler hands out dark-colored helmets and armor for free at night, in exchange for an old story.
Two moons will appear side by side; old records say radiant beasts descend on such nights.
The king danced at the ball in full armor and declared armor the new court formal wear.
A strange light fell from the night sky beyond the northern village; nobody knows what it was.
A survey team reaches the fallen star near the northern village; it still glows red-hot and scorches anyone who comes close.
The fallen star is star-iron, a metal that holds light; smiths forge holy light blades from it and everyone wants one.
The fallen star was an egg; dazzling beasts of light hatch and roam the northern village, and blades are swallowed by their glow.
A dragon egg goes up for auction and a noble wins it with a fortune; the rich start spending wildly.
The dragon egg grows hot and scorches the noble's floors; the household searches for protection that can cool it.
Wrapped in cool protection bought in town, the egg calms; the mother dragon arrives, thanks the town and leaves jewels.
Nothing could cool the egg; the shell cracks and the furious mother dragon circles the town breathing fire.
A black knight challenges the hero to a duel; the hero says they will meet him in first-class gear.
The duel date is set; the black knight's blade is wrapped in darkness and has felled many who lacked the right protection.
The hero wins the duel; the black knight becomes a disciple and fans rush to equip themselves like the hero.
The hero loses; the triumphant black knight gathers an army of darkness, and the kingdom calls for blades of light.
Rats bigger than cats appear under the capital; townsfolk grab whatever they can swing.
The council announces a rat-catching contest with a prize; adventurers arm up to win.
An old woman with three cats wins the contest; humiliated adventurers pawn their weapons.
The rats were familiars of a dark master under the capital; hunters go down to strike it with blades that dispel darkness.
Singing is heard from an abandoned mine at night.
Deep in the mine is a rock spirit that drives off the survey team with fists of stone; axes bounce off it.
Armed with weapons from town, the team calms the spirit; in thanks it opens a rich vein of hard ore and rock-hard armor floods the market.
Lacking the right weapons the team retreats; the angry rock spirit walks out onto the highway.
The crown announces a grand tournament in the capital; fighters gather from everywhere.
A swordsman wreathed in fire sweeps the qualifiers, burning opponents; the hero is to face him.
The hero wins the tournament; fans want the same top-class gear.
The fire swordsman wins; young fighters copy his flaming blade.
A peddler sells magic stones that he swears will only rise in value; people spend savings on stones instead of gear.
Magic-stone fever grips the town; even adventurers sell their good gear to buy more stones.
The peddler vanishes overnight; the magic stones were painted river pebbles and the town is broke.
The stones were real and hold darkness; their owners' shadows start to claw at them.
Snow falls in midsummer.
Cold and ice monsters pour out of {dungeon}; something deep inside is said to be calling winter.
The hero defeats the ice queen deep in {dungeon}; summer returns and the ice monsters melt away.
The hero is driven back; winter settles in and ice monsters from {dungeon} attack the town with freezing water and ice.
